text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

"-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has promised that the party will work alongside the government and people to improve the national education system, whose decade-long deterioration has come in for strong criticism.
-- Qiao Shi, Chairman of the People's National Congress and member of the Standing Committee of China's Politburo, arrived in Hanoi on Sunday for a five-day official visit.
-- South Korea has agreed to provide Vietnam with a $50 million soft loan for the upgrading of the Ba Ria thermal power plant, 100 km north of Ho Chi Minh City.
-- Vietnam exported 231,000 tonnes of coffee during the 1995-1996 crop, up 9.8 percent from the previous crop. last year, and exported $420 million of coffee.
-- Prime minister Tran Duc Luong told reporters that Vietnam's average income per capita would still be below $500 by the year 2000.

-- The Ministry of Planning and Investment has granted investment licences for 35 foreign projects with total capital of more than $918 million in October, the highest level in any one month so far this year.
-- South Korean President Kim Young-sam held talks with the chairman of the Vietnam Journalists Association, Phan Quang, last week.
